title: X-World: Controllable Ego-Centric Multi-Camera World Models for Scalable End-to-End Driving

output_modality.value: future multi-camera video (seven cameras, 12 FPS) generated from multi-view history

control_signal.value: Future ego action sequence; optional controls for dynamic agents and static road elements; text prompt for appearance; camera parameters

control_mechanism.value: Adaptive layer norm for actions and timesteps, additive embeddings for camera parameters, decoupled cross-attention branches for dynamic agents, static elements and text

base_model.value: WAN 2.2 5B latent video model: 3D causal VAE (16x spatial, 4x temporal), customised multi-view DiT with view-temporal self-attention; Stage-II causal few-step streaming with rolling KV cache

datasets.value: Proprietary real-world driving data: 10-second segments with seven synchronised cameras, agent trajectories, static elements and VLM-generated captions

controllability_evidence.value: Qualitative action-controllability figure: logged versus generated video with ego trajectory for next 3 s overlaid (for example Turn Right to Turn Left); no number in packet

closed_loop.value: Yes, as a streaming autoregressive simulator for VLA policies: counterfactual detour and inserted-cyclist examples shown qualitatively; rollout length not stated; training clips are 81 frames

stated_limitations.value: Stage-I bidirectional model needs about 50 sampling steps and generates whole short clips offline, unsuited to low-latency streaming; addressed by Stage-II

notes: Technical report. Metrics and quantitative controllability results are probably in pages missing from the packet. Could also be read as multi-condition control. [metrics: packet mentions a quantitative evaluation protocol but gives no metric names or values]
